docTitle: Scholarships in Europe for Nigerian and African students (2027)

slides.title: Scholarships in Europe for *Nigerian and African* students
slides.sub: Some deadlines have already passed. These are the main ones, with the dates I checked on official sites on 2 November.

slides.title: They don’t all work the *same way*

ways.t: Apply once for both the scholarship and the master’s
Get a university offer, then apply for the scholarship
Two separate applications, one to each

slides.body: Check which way it works before you start any forms.

slides.title: Fully funded or *partial*?

full.v: Your tuition and money to live on every month, like Erasmus Mundus

part.v: Some of it, like €5,000 once from the NL Scholarship

slides.body: Before you apply, check which kind it is and how much you would still pay yourself.

slides.title: *€1,400* a month for up to 24 months
slides.body: It’s the EU scholarship for master’s programmes, open to students from anywhere in the world. Most programmes take applications between October and January.

slides.title: An Erasmus Mundus master’s at my university opens on *2 December*
slides.body: It’s called AISS, and Tallinn University, where I study, is part of it. I got admission and a partial scholarship for it, but I chose another programme.

slides.title: DAAD EPOS needs work experience
slides.body: DAAD EPOS is a German scholarship for development-related master’s courses. A lot of the 2027 deadlines have passed, so if you’re aiming for 2028, start now.

slides.title: The Swedish Institute has *two steps*
slides.body: It pays your tuition and a monthly allowance. It’s for people with work and leadership experience, and Nigeria is on the list.

slides.title: *€5,000* for your first year in the Netherlands
slides.body: The NL Scholarship is for students from outside the EEA, Nigeria included, at Dutch universities that take part.

slides.title: Nigerians can apply for Stipendium Hungaricum
slides.body: It doesn’t cover all your living costs. The 2027/28 round isn’t open yet, and in Nigeria the Department of Scholarship Awards nominates you.

slides.title: Estonia’s state scholarship is not for Nigerians
slides.body: This is where I study. For Nigerians, the realistic options here are these two.

slides.title: Chevening (UK) reopens around *August 2027*
slides.body: It closed on 6 October. The UK isn’t in the EU, but Nigerians do get Chevening, so you can prepare for the next round now.

slides.title: What I’d tell a *friend*
rows: Start preparing a year before you go.
Make a calendar with every deadline and the documents each one needs.
Ask for your official transcripts early, because they take time.
Write a new motivation letter for each programme.
Only apply on the official website.

slides.title: Which one are you applying for?
slides.body: If you apply and get in, please come back and give your testimony.
